title.en: The wind farm at the land's end

text.en: At the southern tip of Tamil Nadu, in Kanniyakumari district, hundreds of giant wind turbines turn all day, and this is the largest concentration of wind farms at a single place in the world. Far to the north, a coal plant burns fuel that took millions of years to form. Same electricity, two very different kinds of energy.

The resources from which electricity is generated are called energy resources, they are the key factor for all economic activity and industrial development, and they are classified as non-renewable or renewable.
Coal is an inflammable organic substance made mainly of hydrocarbons, found in sedimentary rocks, and mostly used to make thermal power.
By carbon content coal is anthracite with 80 to 90 percent, bituminous 60 to 80, lignite 40 to 60 and peat below 40 percent.
Indian coal is mostly in Gondwana rocks of the peninsula, and Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh together hold nearly 90 percent of the reserves, with Jharkhand the largest producer.
About 2 percent of Indian coal is tertiary coal found in Assam and Jammu and Kashmir, and lignite or brown coal is found in Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Kerala, mined by NLC India at Neyveli.
Coal India Limited at Kolkata, NLC India and Singareni Collieries are the public sector companies in coal.
The word petroleum comes from the Latin petro, meaning rock, and oleum, meaning oil, so it is mineral oil, with hydrocarbons forming 90 to 95 percent of it.
Petroleum powers automobiles, aeroplanes, ships and locomotives, and gives lubricants, kerosene, vaseline, tar, wax, soap and terylene as by-products.
Offshore, the Mumbai High field is the largest with about 65 percent of output, the Gujarat coast is second, and the Bassein field lies south of Mumbai High.
Onshore, the Brahmaputra valley in Upper Assam has the Digboi field, the oldest in the country, along with Nahorkatiya and Moran-Hugrijan.
Natural gas usually comes with petroleum, is mainly methane, and is used for heating, cooking, electricity and as vehicle fuel in the form of CNG; GAIL of New Delhi is the largest state-owned gas company.
Thermal power uses coal, diesel, petroleum and natural gas, NTPC was set up in 1975, and in Tamil Nadu the important thermal stations are Neyveli, Mettur, Thoothukudi and Ennore.
Nuclear energy comes from the fission of uranium and thorium; the first station was at Tarapur near Mumbai in 1969, and others are at Rawatbhata, Kalpakkam with 440 MW, Kudankulam with 2000 MW, Narora, Kaiga and Kakrapara.
Hydropower from running water is economic and non-polluting, the first hydro station was at Darjeeling in 1897, and NHPC is located at Faridabad.
Solar energy turns sunlight into electricity by photovoltaic cells or by concentrated solar power, and Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh are the major producers.
Wind energy is cheap and pollution free; wind farms began in India in 1986 at Okha, Ratnagiri and Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu has the largest installation, and Muppandal-Aralvoimozhi in Kanniyakumari is the biggest wind farm concentration in the world.
Biomass energy comes from dung, kitchen waste, water hyacinth and crop residue, while tidal energy is best suited to the Gulf of Cambay, then the Gulf of Kutch and the Sunderbans, and a 150 kW wave power plant stands at Vizhinjam near Thiruvananthapuram.

problem.en: A coal sample has 65 percent carbon and another has 45 percent. Name each type and say which gives more heat.

text.en: Check the carbon ranges: bituminous 60 to 80, lignite 40 to 60.

why.en: Coal type is decided by carbon content.

text.en: 65 percent falls in the bituminous range and 45 percent in the lignite range.

why.en: Match each number to its range.

text.en: The bituminous coal has more carbon, so it is the better and hotter fuel.

why.en: More carbon means more energy per kilogram.

prompt.en: Explain why a country should use both renewable and non-renewable energy today, and name one example of each from Tamil Nadu.

requiredIdeas.en: Non-renewable resources such as coal cannot be replaced, for example lignite at Neyveli
Renewable resources regenerate, for example wind at Muppandal
Renewables are clean and cheap to run, while coal and gas give steady large power for industry

commonMisconceptions.en: Nuclear energy is renewable (it uses uranium and thorium, which are non-renewable)
Hydropower pollutes a lot (it is considered non-polluting)

points.en: Non-renewable: coal, petroleum, natural gas, nuclear minerals; renewable: water, sun, wind, biomass, tides.
Coal ranks anthracite, bituminous, lignite, peat by carbon; Jharkhand leads output.
Mumbai High is the largest oil field; Digboi the oldest; Tarapur the first nuclear plant (1969).
Tamil Nadu: Neyveli lignite, Kudankulam nuclear and Muppandal wind.
